name: Sucralfate
route_note: Oral tablets or suspension, usually before meals and at bedtime

discovery.note: A basic aluminium salt of sucrose octasulfate developed as a non-systemic ulcer-healing agent. Year of Chugai's first preparation reports and patents (Nametaka et al., Yakugaku Zasshi 1967; US 3,432,489), per the Merck Index.

tagline: Non-absorbed aluminium-sucrose complex that coats and protects ulcers
summary: Sucralfate is an aluminium complex of sulfated sucrose that forms a protective barrier over ulcer craters. It acts locally with minimal absorption and is used for duodenal ulcers and, in some settings, stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
mechanism: In acid, sucralfate polymerises into a viscous paste that binds positively charged proteins exposed in the ulcer base, forming a barrier against acid, pepsin and bile salts.

It also adsorbs pepsin and bile acids, stimulates local prostaglandin and bicarbonate production, and binds epidermal growth factor at the ulcer site. It does not substantially change gastric acid output.
uses: Maintenance therapy after healing of duodenal ulcer
Stress-ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill patients (some settings)

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Carafate tablets for duodenal ulcer.

history.title: Stress ulcer risk factors
history.detail: Large Canadian study defines risk factors for ICU stress-ulcer bleeding, informing prophylaxis choices.

history.title: ICU trial
history.detail: A randomised trial (Cook et al., NEJM) finds ranitidine more effective than sucralfate in preventing GI bleeding in ventilated patients.

pk.bioavailability: <5% (sucrose sulfate); small amounts of aluminium absorbed
pk.excretion: Mostly faeces; absorbed fraction in urine

serious: Reduced absorption of other drugs (e.g. fluoroquinolones, warfarin, digoxin, levothyroxine)

facts: Other medicines are usually taken at least two hours apart from sucralfate because it binds them in the gut.
Sucralfate requires an acidic environment to polymerise and adhere to the mucosa.
